approach: Add a pure `check(&Comparison) -> Vec<Gap>` in a new crates/athena-core/src/comparison.rs, modelled on mechanism_explanation.rs. A `Comparison` holds shared concepts (each with per-system entries), mechanism comparisons (each with per-system entries) and an optional essay. The three systems come from the existing `crate::lab::SYSTEMS` (lab.rs:25). Gaps come out in a fixed order: concepts, comparisons, essay. The essay must be non-blank, at most a documented word cap, and mention both `prompt` and `orchestrat` (case-insensitive). Declare the module in lib.rs between `commits` and `context_load`. Add tests/comparison.rs in the S4-01 test shape: complete and defective inputs, plus the real docs/spec.toml entry read through `parse_spec`, `measure_problem` and `spec_gaps`. Fill the S7-01 mechanism and measure in docs/spec.toml, ending `status: not shown`. Add a CHANGELOG bullet. Add one line to xtask/shard-timings.txt: it is outside the listed deliverables but required, because a new test target without that line fails `cargo test --locked` (see decision 4). Every public type derives Debug, because the workspace sets `missing_debug_implementations = "warn"` and the checks run clippy with `-D warnings` (Cargo.toml:60).

decisions.choice: Input is one `Comparison` record with concepts, mechanism comparisons and an optional essay; `check(&Comparison) -> Vec<Gap>`. Both concepts and comparisons hold `Entry { system, text }` lists, so one entry type serves both.
decisions.reason: The requirement concerns one study with one closing essay. A single record lets the check report NoConcepts, NoComparisons and NoEssay as gaps. S4-01's slice input cannot report an empty input (mechanism_explanation.rs:12). One shared `Entry` type keeps the module small.

rejected.why: An empty slice would give no gaps, so 'no concepts' and 'no comparisons' could not be reported.

rejected.option: Read the study's files from disk
rejected.why: That is wiring into the study capability, which is out of scope. The check stays pure and reads nothing.

decisions.choice: Reuse `crate::lab::SYSTEMS` as the list of the three systems instead of defining a new const.
decisions.reason: Documented meaning at crates/athena-core/src/lab.rs:24-25: 'The three systems every lab configuration must cap.' `["athena", "firstmate", "hermes"]`. The requirement's 'all three systems' are those same systems, and a grep of crates/**/src finds `"firstmate"` only there (one definition). Matching is case-insensitive on the system name. An entry counts only when its system is in the list and its text is not blank. Entries for other names are ignored and never satisfy a required system. lab.rs is not modified.

rejected.why: It duplicates the only list of the three systems, so the two could drift.

rejected.option: Take the system names as a parameter of `check`
rejected.why: No caller needs it. It would make the three-system rule optional.

decisions.choice: The measure ends `status: not shown` and names `cargo test -p athena-core --test comparison`. `measure_problem` accepts a label that starts with `not shown` (hestia.rs:1229).
decisions.reason: No real three-system study exists and nothing runs `check` on one. S3-01, S3-02 and S4-01 use the same wording (spec.toml:2994 is the S4-01 form).

rejected.why: Nothing in `athena status` reports on this check, so the label would be false.

decisions.reason: `checked_in_timings_cover_every_workspace_test_unit` (xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:410-421) asserts that the set of units in the timings file equals the workspace's test targets (`oracle()`, ci_shards.rs:153-168, which includes every `tests/*.rs` file, see `discovered_sources` at 171-191). The deliverable `crates/athena-core/tests/comparison.rs` adds a target, so without the line `cargo test --locked` (acceptance criterion 4) fails. The mirrors registry reports the same drift: `Rule::TimingUnits` (mirrors.rs:58-59, 116-119) and `missing_timing_lines` (mirrors.rs:206-227), run on the real repo by `the_real_repo_has_no_mirror_drift` (crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs:22). The previous S4-01 landing touched this file too (HISTORY.txt lines 44-51). The file is a data file of estimated seconds, not athena.toml, defaults.toml, a workflow or lint configuration. Order in the file is free: lines 52-60 are not sorted, and both checks build a set. This corrects the earlier plan's 'alphabetical' claim.

rejected.option: Leave the timings file out because it is not a listed deliverable
rejected.why: The new test target would fail ci_shards.rs:410-421 and the mirrors check, so criterion 4 would fail.

rejected.option: Put the tests in comparison.rs unit tests so no new test target exists
rejected.why: The brief lists tests/comparison.rs as a deliverable and the measure names `--test comparison`.

decisions.choice: The essay topic is matched by a case-insensitive substring test for both `prompt` and `orchestrat` in the essay text. 'Short' is `ESSAY_WORD_CAP = 800` whitespace-separated words, so 800 passes and 801 fails. Both are documented in the `Limits:` list and in the measure.
decisions.reason: The requirement says 'a short essay on building orchestration from prompts'. A word count and two terms are a cheap, deterministic proxy, stated as a proxy as S4-01 does for 'primary'. A blank or absent essay is `NoEssay` and returns before the other essay gaps. A non-blank essay can give both `EssayTooLong` and `EssayOffTopic`, in that order.

rejected.option: Compare a topic label field to a fixed string
rejected.why: A label the study sets itself would check nothing about the essay's content.
A pure check cannot. The Limits list says so.

decisions.reason: `crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs:1-2` runs request and reading shapes through the reading gate (`refusing_check`). The new topic match is a substring test inside a pure function over a study record, not a parser, stem list, stop list or reading check, and nothing in the gate calls it. The input forms it handles are mixed case, `orchestrating`, only one of the two terms, and whitespace-only text. Each is a unit test in tests/comparison.rs.

rejected.option: Add corpus cases for the essay terms
rejected.why: The corpus drives the reading gate, which this check is not part of.

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/comparison.rs. The module doc starts `OLY-B-S7-01: ...` and has a plain-text `Limits:` list: a mapping or comparison counts when it names a system and has non-blank text, and a concept or mechanism the study leaves out is not detected; 'short' is at most 800 whitespace-separated words; the topic is a case-insensitive match for `prompt` and `orchestrat`; nothing yet feeds `check` a real three-system study, so the spec measure ends `status: not shown`. Add `use crate::lab::SYSTEMS;`, `pub const ESSAY_WORD_CAP: usize = 800;` and the match terms. Add the types, all `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]`: `Entry { system, text }`, `Concept { name, entries }`, `MechanismComparison { mechanism, entries }`, `Essay { text }` and `Comparison { concepts, comparisons, essay: Option<Essay> }`. Add `enum Gap { NoConcepts, ConceptMissingSystem{concept, system}, NoComparisons, ComparisonMissingSystem{mechanism, system}, NoEssay, EssayTooLong{words, cap}, EssayOffTopic }`. Implement `check` in fixed order: concepts first (NoConcepts if empty, else a gap per concept per missing system in SYSTEMS order), then comparisons the same way, then the essay (absent or blank gives NoEssay and nothing else; otherwise EssayTooLong, then EssayOffTopic). An entry satisfies a system only when its name matches one in SYSTEMS (ignore ASCII case) and its text is not blank.

Edit crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs: add `pub mod comparison;` between `pub mod commits;` (line 110) and `pub mod context_load;` (line 111), and add a crate-doc bullet after the `mechanism_explanation` bullet (lines 48-49) for OLY-B-S7-01 saying it is a pure function not wired into any command.

Create crates/athena-core/tests/comparison.rs from the S4-01 test shape (tests/mechanism_explanation.rs): `repo_file`, `owner_problem`, `measure_label_problem`, `real_requirement`, with REQUIREMENT `OLY-B-S7-01` and TEST_COMMAND `cargo test -p athena-core --test comparison`, plus builders for entries, concepts, comparisons and essays. Tests: complete gives no gaps; each missing system in a concept (all three systems); each missing system in a mechanism comparison; no concepts; no comparisons; absent essay; blank essay; 801-word essay gives EssayTooLong and 800 words passes; essay missing `orchestrat`, essay missing `prompt`, mixed-case and `orchestrating` pass; blank entry text does not count; unknown system name does not count; extra entries are ignored; several defects give gaps in order; comparison.rs's doc comment contains `Limits:`; `spec_entry_has_a_real_mechanism`; the four negative spec-helper tests.

Edit line 3039 to a measure: the test file checks complete and defective comparisons and this spec entry; Limits (mapping and comparison presence, the 800-word cap, the `prompt`/`orchestrat` match, a concept or mechanism left out is not detected, `check` not yet run on a real three-system study); then `cargo test -p athena-core --test comparison; status: not shown`. Keep `owner = "Athena"` and change nothing else.

Add a CHANGELOG.md bullet under [Unreleased] > Added, before line 12's bullet, in the S4-01 style: the mechanism (`check` in comparison.rs), the test command, the limits including the 800-word cap and that nothing runs it on a real study, and the shard-timings registration.
Add `athena-core --test comparison 5.00` to xtask/shard-timings.txt next to the `mechanism_explanation` line (line 60).

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-core --test comparison`, `cargo test -p xtask --test ci_shards`, `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` and `cargo test --locked`.
